reading: A reader deciding in thirty seconds whether this plugin is for them: the first screen answers what it is, what it does to their text, and why they would want it; everything else follows in the order a decision needs.
A reader who has a document they doubt and wants to know what to type first: the document is organised around the first action and what comes back from it, and each skill is a thing they run.
A reader who fears a tool that rewrites their text: the document is organised around control — what it reads, what it writes, where, and when it asks — and the assurances come before any capability.

A reader who already uses a linter, a style guide or an AI writing assistant: the document positions the plugin against those — what it is not, what it measures that they do not — and the sections follow the comparison.

A maintainer of a large documentation tree who has been burned by rewrites that made things worse: the document is organised around iteration — rounds, the ledger, regression as the enemy — and shows how a change is proven before it lands.

A writer who is not a programmer — prose, comments, a course, a policy — and reads no CLI jargon: the document speaks of text, readers and improvement, and confines every command to one block they copy.

The genre as the vendor and the popular plugins have converged on it: what the marketplace listing expects — install, the skills as a table, what each returns — in the order N of M surveyed documents use.
The pipeline itself as the spine: one picture of audit → rethink → rewrite → audit again, and every section is a stage of it, in the order the stages run, with what enters and what leaves each.
A sceptical reader who trusts only what was measured: every claim about what the plugin does sits beside how it was measured and its limits, and the document's own honesty is its argument.
The shortest document that satisfies the purpose statement — at most four hundred words — where every section must justify its place against a reader who stops after the first screen.
